_about: PRO batch 40: era 4, The Veteran (34-37), set 1.

scenarios.title: The Mentor's Funeral
scenarios.text: The veteran who taught you the most in your rookie year, the one whose job you took, has died. His family asks if you'll be a pallbearer.

choices.label: Carry him
choices.result: You carry him, with five of his old teammates, in a small church full of football players. His wife tells you he followed every kick you ever made.

choices.label: Tell his story to the rookies
choices.result: His story, told to every rookie specialist in the building: how he taught the kid who replaced him. It becomes a tradition in your locker room.

choices.label: Write to his family
choices.result: A long letter to his family, about the hour he spent teaching you on your first day. They read it at the reception.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Clinic
scenarios.text: You run your first coaching clinic for high school kickers, forty of them, on a muddy field, and by noon you realize you might be good at this.

choices.label: Teach every kid one thing
choices.result: One thing for every kid, all forty, by name. Two of them fix their plant foot by lunch, and you can't stop grinning.

choices.label: Run it like a pro camp
choices.result: Stations, charts, film on a laptop under a tent. The parents are amazed, and three college coaches ask for your notes.

choices.label: Keep it fun
choices.result: Games, contests, a lot of laughing. The kids leave in love with kicking, and you leave with a sunburn and an idea.

scenarios.title: The Broadcast Audition
scenarios.text: The network wants an audition tape for the broadcast booth: three minutes, a desk, a monitor. Your agent wants you to keep kicking and not think about it yet.

choices.label: Make the tape
choices.result: The tape, made in a studio on your day off. You're stiff for one minute and good for two, and the network calls back within a week.

choices.label: Wait until you're done
choices.result: After football, you tell the network. They say the door stays open, and your agent sends a thumbs-up and three exclamation points.

choices.label: Ask {tyler} to help
choices.result: {tyler}, already in the booth, spends an evening coaching you on the tape. He's a ruthless teacher, and the tape is very good.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Job, Part-Time
scenarios.text: A college asks you to coach its kickers in the offseason while you're still playing: three months, a small office, and twelve kickers who've watched you for years.

choices.label: Take the job
choices.result: Three offseason months, coaching. You're exhausted by camp and better at your own craft for having explained it every day.

choices.label: Do it one day a week
choices.result: One day a week, Fridays only. The kickers get the best of you, and your own training doesn't suffer at all.

choices.label: Not while you're playing
choices.result: Not while you're still playing, you tell them. They understand, and the head coach says the job will be there when you're ready.

scenarios.title: The Foundation at Ten
scenarios.text: Your foundation turns ten this year. Some of the kids from its very first program are in college now, and three of them want to speak at the anniversary dinner.

choices.label: Let the kids speak
choices.result: The three of them, at the podium, telling their own stories. Nobody in the room is dry-eyed by the end, including you.

choices.label: Plan the next ten years
choices.result: The next ten years, planned with the board in a long, hopeful meeting. The foundation doubles its programs by spring.

choices.label: Keep it small and personal
choices.result: A small dinner, just the first year's kids and their families. It's the best night the foundation has ever had, and nobody takes photos.

scenarios.title: The Record Book
scenarios.text: You're three kicks away from a club record nobody thought a kicker would ever hold, and the countdown is on the stadium's video board every week.

choices.label: Ignore the countdown
choices.result: No looking at the board, no reading, no talking about it. When it finally happens, you find out from {holder}, who is crying.

choices.label: Share it with the unit
choices.result: Every interview turns to the snapper and {holder}. When the record falls, the three of you hold the ball together for the photo.

choices.label: Let yourself want it
choices.result: For once, you let yourself want it. It's fun, and nerve-racking, and you sleep badly for three weeks and don't regret it.

scenarios.title: Hall of Fame Talk
scenarios.text: A columnist writes that you belong in the Hall of Fame. Another columnist writes, the next day, that kickers never do. Your phone has opinions about both.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.result: No comment, on either column. The argument goes on without you for a week, and you kick better for staying out of it.

choices.label: Make the case for kickers
choices.result: A calm, funny answer at your locker about what kickers actually do. It's the clip of the week, and three old kickers call to thank you.

choices.label: Laugh about it at home
choices.result: Both columns, read out loud at dinner in funny voices. Your family votes you in unanimously, and {parent} frames the good one.

scenarios.title: Your Number at the High School
scenarios.text: Your high school wants to retire your number at the homecoming game, on the field where you learned to kick, with the whole town in the stands.

choices.label: Walk out with {parent}
choices.result: Out onto the field with {parent} beside you, under the lights. The crowd stands, and {parent} squeezes your arm so hard it leaves a mark.

choices.label: Give the number to a kid
choices.result: The number, retired, and then handed to the current team's kicker for one night. He kicks with your number, and the town goes wild.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: A wave, a handshake with the principal, and back to the stands. You watch the rest of the game with your old friends.

choices.label: Ask your old coach to present it
choices.result: Your old high school coach, gray now, hands you the framed jersey. He doesn't say a word, and he doesn't have to.
choices.lock_text: having earned your high school coach's trust

scenarios.title: The Documentary
scenarios.text: A filmmaker wants to follow you for a whole season: the facility, your home, your hotel rooms, the hard days. She's made two documentaries you love.

choices.label: Say yes to all of it
choices.result: All of it, on camera. The film is honest and beautiful, and it shows you some things about yourself you'd rather not have seen.

choices.label: Set limits
choices.result: Yes, with rules: no home, no family, no hotel rooms. The film is smaller and still good, and your kids stay out of it.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: No, politely, with thanks. A season is a long time to be watched, and you'd rather have this one to yourself and your family.

scenarios.title: The All-Decade Team
scenarios.text: The league is naming its all-decade team, and the vote for kicker is close: you and a younger kicker with a stronger leg and better highlights.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: Not a word, not a campaign. You find out from your agent at breakfast, and either way, you finish your eggs.

choices.label: Congratulate the other kicker early
choices.result: A message to the other kicker before the vote, honest and kind. Whoever wins, the two of you have dinner the next time your clubs play.

choices.label: Let yourself hope
choices.result: For a week, you let yourself hope out loud. It's fun, and you laugh at yourself for caring this much at your age.

scenarios.title: The Body Decides
scenarios.text: A doctor clips an X-ray to the light box and points at your hip. The choice about how long you keep playing, she says carefully, may not be yours much longer.

choices.label: Ask for every option
choices.result: Every option, laid out on paper: surgery, rest, a season more, a season less. You take the paper home and read it with {love_interest} until midnight.

choices.label: Get a second opinion
choices.result: A second opinion, a week later, from a specialist two states away. He says the same thing in fewer words, and you thank him for it.

choices.label: Keep kicking for now
choices.result: For now, you keep kicking, carefully. The doctor writes something in your file and asks you to come back in a month.

scenarios.title: The Recovery Clinic
scenarios.text: A recovery clinic promises to make your veteran leg feel ten years younger. The brochure is beautiful, two veterans swear by it, and the treatment menu includes a substance the league bans.

choices.label: Walk out of the consultation
choices.result: Out of the consultation, politely, before the second page. You tell the team doctor about the clinic, and she thanks you and adds it to a list.

choices.label: Ask the team doctor for a real plan
choices.result: A real plan from the team doctor: legal, slow and specific. Your leg doesn't feel ten years younger, and by October it feels strong, honest and your own.

choices.label: Book the full program
choices.result: The forms for the full program, signed in the clinic's leather chair. Three weeks later the league's testers are waiting at the facility on a Tuesday morning, and your name is first on their list.

scenarios.title: Young Again
scenarios.text: The young players go out every night after home games, and they keep inviting you, like you're one of them. Tonight they've booked a booth somewhere loud, and they're chanting your name.

choices.label: Dinner with them, then home
choices.result: Dinner with them, and the best stories you've got. You're home by eleven, and they call you 'unc' with real affection at Monday's meeting.

choices.label: Invite them to your house instead
choices.result: Your house, Sunday afternoon, a grill and the kids running around. Half the young players come, and it becomes a monthly thing.

choices.label: Go out with them
choices.result: Out with them, until three. Your hip hates you on Monday, a photo of the night ends up online, and {coach} wants to talk before the meeting.
